title: Read Nucleus output and execution history
summary: Read exact retained harness observations and derive correlated structured output without rerunning a job.
use_when: A selected job's runtime history, final message, raw output, or historical decoder evidence must be inspected.
do_not_use_when: The goal is to establish requester-domain success, obtain authentication output, or use stored billing projections.
outcome: Retained runtime observations and any supported correlated structured output are returned for the selected job.
effects: Reads expose retained prompts, source content, tool values, and runtime diagnostics; they do not execute another attempt.
authority: Nucleus owns exact received output observations and operational execution records.
Requesters own domain results; reporting consumers own interpretations, totals, coverage, and prices.
success: The requested retained output is returned with identities and sequence, or missing structured evidence remains explicitly unavailable.
failure_and_recovery: A decoder repair can recover derived output from retained evidence without rewriting atoms or terminal state. Missing records cannot be recovered or treated as permission to retry.
privacy: Nucleus private state can contain complete prompts, source content, tool arguments and results, exact harness output, and terminal diagnostics. Keep state and logs private.

interfaces.label: Read a decoder schema
interfaces.invocation: GET /v1/schemas/{schema} over the Nucleus Unix socket

does_not_authorize: Requester-domain acceptance, replay of failed work, credential disclosure, or deletion of retained data.

consumers.statement: Operators and requester/reporting consumers may inspect retained job state, exact output observations, and supported derived final output.

preconditions.statement: Select the exact job or requester run and use supported read interfaces; retained evidence must support any structured projection.

inputs.statement: Reads use exact job IDs, requester program/ID filters, per-attempt numeric output cursors, follow=true, or exact generated schema IDs.

outputs.statement: The version-one log envelope exposes jobId, attemptId, sequence, observedAt, stream=harness.output, schemaId, payload, and payloadDigest. Completed attempts can expose threadId, turnId, and finalMessage.
Failed, cancelled, timed-out, and lost attempts expose no successful structured output. Authentication responses and stderr chunks are not output records.

data_semantics.statement: Each atom preserves one received non-authentication harness stdout JSONL payload with only its line delimiter removed. Operational records remain separate from reporting observations.

Read-time projection binds only the retained successful empty MCP-inventory startup sequence and its correlated thread/turn messages, freezing at that turn's terminal notification. Missing or conflicting startup evidence produces no structured output.

identity_and_units.statement: Sequence orders atoms within one attempt; observedAt is Nucleus observation time rather than ordering authority. The public digest covers public payload bytes.

Malformed/non-UTF-8 bytes or JSON whose whitespace would be lost use the reversible nucleus.raw-bytes.v1 base64 envelope. The failure terminalMessage is control-character sanitized and capped at 16 KiB.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Nucleus retains every non-authentication stdout JSONL record it receives. Host-managed authentication responses and managed-worker stderr are excluded; raw input and lifecycle/control events are not reporting atoms.
Bounded follow returns one output-only LogsResponseV1 page. Status reads mailbox and job state successively, not atomically. Initial read errors remain errors.
No output-arrival, retention-horizon, billing, or completeness beyond received non-authentication observations is promised.

access.statement: The supported standard surfaces are the current-user CLI and version-one HTTP protocol over Nucleus's filesystem-protected Unix socket.
Local filesystem ownership and permissions protect the socket and private state; version one has no application-level authentication protocol.
No TCP endpoint, cross-user service, catalog-granted access, or direct SQLite integration is supported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The exact generated harness schema remains available for decoding. Derived output uses retained authentication startup evidence, not today's account mode: response IDs 1/2/3 for API-key inventory/thread/turn and 2/3/4 for managed authentication.
A decoder repair can expose supported output when an old completed job is read again without a new attempt, changed raw observations, or changed terminal state.

operational_limits.statement: One attempt per version-one job makes its numeric log cursor unambiguous. Nucleus stores no reporting totals, usage prices, final-output materialization, or stderr stream.
No automatic pruning, output-volume bound, or database-retention period is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: The version-one log envelope remains compatible; exact harness schema and retained invocation evidence select historical decoding. Store, adapter, provider, and feature versions remain separate.
No general historical-decoder retirement window is promised.

reliances.statement: Received messages and their schema semantics originate in the exact adapter-proved Codex app-server contract, which has no installed Chancery contract. Retained reads do not invoke Codex again.
